operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 9894, signed September 23, 1947, which orders that the San Clemente Island Naval Defensive Sea Area, established by Executive Order 7747 as amended by Executive Orders 8536 and 9787, be and is hereby discontinued. It states no delayed effective date, so the effective date is the signing date, 1947-09-23 (the order was published September 25, 1947, the alternative reading). Executive Order 9787 restated Executive Order 7747 to read as follows: it established the defensive sea area, barred vessels from navigating within it except as authorized by the Secretary of the Navy, and set the penalties provided by law for violations. All three provisions depend on the existence of the area and ended when the area was discontinued.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER 9787
Amendment  of E xecutive  O rder N o. 7747 
of  N ovember 20, 1937, as A mended , E s­
tablishing  th e S an C lemente  I sland 
N aval D efensive  S ea A rea
Executive Order No. 7747 of November 
20,1937, as aménded by Executive Order 
No. 8536 of September 6, 1940, is hereby 
amended to read as follows;
“By virtue of and pursuant to the 
authority vested in me by the provisions 
of section 44 of the Criminal Code, as 
amended (18 U. S. C. 96), the area of 
water surrounding San Clemente Island, 
California, extending from low-water 
mark out for a distance of three hundred 
yards beyond low-water mark, except in 
Wilson Cove, where it is to extend one 
huhdred yards beyond low-water mark, 
and including that part of Pyramid Cove 
lying north of a line between a point 
one thousand yards south of China Point 
light and a point three hundred yards 
south of Whitewashed Rock, is hereby 
established as a defensive sea area for 
purposes of national defense, subject to 
the uses reserved for the Department of 
Commerce by Executive Order No. 6897 of 
November 7, 1934. The said area shall 
be known as the San Clemente Island 
Naval Defensive Sea Area.
“At no time shall vessels or other craft 
be navigated within the defensive sea 
area above defined except such as are 
authorized by the Secretary of the Navy.
“Any person violating the provisions of 
this order shall be subject to the penalties 
provided by law.”

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (11 FR 11556) is Executive Order 9787 amending Executive Order 7747, with its heading, recital and the quoted restated order read in full. Inventory read and confirmed: one clause, the amending lead-in and the restated order (area, navigation bar, penalty), all of which fall with the area. End: Executive Order 9894 (12 FR 6353) discontinues the area by name, citing Executive Order 9787 among the orders that established it. The packet lacks an acting-provision record for Executive Order 9894, so the ending source cited is its full held text. Prior research: none reported. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete with no coverage warning. The six own-term records in the dossier come from neighboring orders printed on the same page (a Civil Aeronautics Board notice and a claims regulation) and are not terms of this order.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Executive Order 9787 has no end date or termination clause. The dossier's chain of later events is empty because the acting provision of Executive Order 9894 was not located by the machine, but I read the held text of Executive Order 9894: it discontinues the whole area on its signing date. Citations of Executive Order 9787 by number in other held texts are limited to the neighboring Federal Register pages; no earlier discontinuance, revocation or boundary change appears in the three selected machine searches or the dossier.","independent_command_check":"The navigation restriction and the penalty provision exist only within the defensive sea area. The authority they rest on (section 44 of the Criminal Code, 18 U.S.C. 96) is a statute that the order applied; it does not itself restrict navigation in this area. No independent command survives the discontinuance.","savings_check":"Executive Order 9894 has no saving clause and no held source shows a surviving effect. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; possible liability for earlier violations is noted but not established.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried although it contains three provisions (establishment of the area, restriction on navigation, penalty); they are inseparable parts of one restated order and all end with the discontinuance of the area. Executive Order 9894 discontinues the area as a whole, not a part."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 9894 is a one-sentence discontinuance with no saving clause. Liability for violations committed before the discontinuance is not addressed by any held source; no continuing regulation or transferred function is shown.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12292 (signed February 23, 1981), section 10(b) of which revokes Executive Order 9799 of November 8, 1946. Section 11 of Executive Order 12292 states that it is effective as of February 15, 1981, which is therefore the effective date of the revocation; the alternative reading is that the revocation operated from signing on 1981-02-23 or publication on 1981-02-25. February 15, 1981 is also the date the Foreign Service Act of 1980 took effect (section 2403(a)), repealing the 1946 Act whose section 411 power the order delegated; section 2401(a) of the 1980 Act continued orders issued under the 1946 Act until revoked or superseded, so the repeal by itself did not end the order and the express revocation is the end. The order authorized and directed the Secretary of State to exercise the President's power under section 411 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 to classify chief-of-mission positions into four classes, effective November 13, 1946. The label EO 9452 attached to one acting record in the dossier is the Federal Register issue holding Executive Order 12292, not an earlier revoking order.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (11 FR, November 13, 1946) is Executive Order 9799 signed November 8, 1946 (read in full). Inventory read and confirmed: one delegating clause with its effective-date sentence. End: Executive Order 12292 section 10(b), effective as of February 15, 1981 under its section 11; the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (public law 96-465, held in the source-ladder queue text) repealed the 1946 Act effective the same day (section 2205 with section 2403(a)) but continued issued orders until revoked or superseded (section 2401(a)), which is why the revocation, not the repeal, is claimed as the end. This closes the gap noted in prior research. Prior research: two earlier Astra claim versions for this order differ on later_events and neither is canonical; their reported gap (actual repeal, savings and effective-date terms of the 1980 Act) is addressed here. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order has no fixed end date. I examined the repeal of the 1946 Act by the Foreign Service Act of 1980: the repeal took effect February 15, 1981 (section 2403(a)), the same day as the revocation, and section 2401(a) kept orders issued under the 1946 Act in force until revoked, so it is not an earlier end. The dossier's chain also lists an acting record labeled EO 9452 dated 1944-06-26; that is a labeling artifact of the Federal Register issue that prints Executive Order 12292 (EO 9452 predates this order and cannot revoke it). No other revoking instrument appears in the three selected machine searches.","independent_command_check":"The delegation depended on section 411 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946, now replaced by section 401 of the 1980 Act, which supplies its own classification power; the order contains no independent regulation or duty. Section 2401(a) of the 1980 Act is a statutory continuation of orders, not an independent command of this order.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12292 was read at sections 2, 10 and 11; savings rest on section 2(c) of that order and sections 2401(a) and 2403(a) of the 1980 Act. Savings state transferred_or_accrued.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole order, a single delegation of the President's classification power for chief-of-mission positions plus its effective-date sentence. Executive Order 12292 section 10(b) revokes the order by number as a whole."}

savings_residuals.reason: Executive Order 12292 contains no saving clause for this order, but section 2(c) of that order treats section 401 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 as the replacement for section 411 of the 1946 Act, and section 2401(a) of the 1980 Act continued determinations and orders made under the 1946 Act until modified, revoked or superseded. Classifications of chief-of-mission positions made under the delegation are accrued consequences; the delegation itself ended with the revocation.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. In the held text of Executive Order 12553 the number 9918 appears in the number column of the first table page, and the aligned entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) describes an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes in the plural, matching this order's title. This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Alabama, Tennessee and Northern Railroad Company and other carriers named in List A and certain of their employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of December 31, 1947 (due by January 30, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

WHEREAS disputes exist between the 
Alabama, Tennessee and Northern Rail­
road Company and certain other car­
riers designated in list A attached hereto 
and made a part hereof, and certain of 
their employees represented by the 
seventeen cooperating nonoperating la­
bor organizations’ designated in list B

and
WHEREAS these disputes have not 
heretofore been adjusted under the pro­
visions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the 
judgment of the National Mediation 
Board, threaten substantially to inter­
rupt interstate commerce to a -degree 
such as to deprive the country of essen­
tial transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I  hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said disputes.
Each of the carriers involved shall be 
given independent consideration in such 
investigation, and the said labor organi­
zations shall be permitted to function
FEDERAL REGISTER
as a unit in proceedings before the 
board.
No member of the said board shall be 
pecuniarily or otherwise interested in 
any organization of railway employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
disputes within thirty days from the 
date of this order. The report of the 
board shall contain separate and inde­
pendent findings with respect to each of 
the carriers involved.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by any of the carriers involved or 
their employees in the conditions out of 
which the said disputes arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. In the held text of Executive Order 12553 the number 9923 appears in the number column of the first table page, and the aligned entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, matching this order's title. This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of January 13, 1948 (due by February 12, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

C reating  an  E m ergency B oard- T o  I n v e s­

WHEREAS a dispute exists between *  
The Akron &  Barberton Belt Railroad, a 
carrier, and certain of its employees rep­
resented by the Brotherhood of Railroad  
Trainmen, a labor organization; and  
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce within the state O f  
Ohio, to a degree such as to deprive that  
portion of the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me,  
to investigate said dispute. No member  
of the said board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said dis­
pute within thirty days from the date ,  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by The Akron &  Barberton Belt  
Railroad or its employees in the condi­
tions out of which the said dispute arose.

Identity: the held Federal Register text is the order itself (heading and body read in full; signed January 13, 1948). Inventory read and confirmed (correction only where stated). End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete with no coverage warning.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (February 12, 1948, thirty days after signing on January 13, 1948) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (recitals, creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). Signature, date line and any attached list identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence of Executive Order 12553."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. In the held text of Executive Order 12553 the number 9929 appears in the number column of the first table page, and the aligned entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, matching this order's title. This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Akron, Canton & Youngstown Railroad Company and other carriers named in the attached list and certain of their employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of January 27, 1948 (due by February 26, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

UNITED STATES STANDARDS FOR FRESH 
SPINACH LEAVES
On December 27, 1947, notice of pro­
posed rule making was published in the 
F ederal  R egister  (12 F . R . 8843) regard­
ing the proposed issuance of United 
States Consumer Standards for Fresh 
Spinach Leaves. After consideration of 
all relevant matters presented, including 
the proposals set forth in the aforesaid 
notice, the following United States Con­
sumer Standards for Fresh Spinach 
Leaves are hereby promulgated pursuant 
to the provisions of the Department of 
Agriculture Appropriation Act, 1948 
(Pub. Law 266, 80th Cong., 1st Sess., ap­
proved Jifty 30, 1947) :
§  51.394 Consumer standards for fresh  
spinach leaves —(a) Grades. (1) U. S. 
Grade A shall consist of spinach leaves 
of similar varietal characteristics which 
are fresh, clean, well trimmed., and of 
reasonably good green color, and which 
are free from coarse stalks, seedstems, 
seedbuds, crowns and roots, sandburs or 
other kinds of burs, soft rot and from 
damage caused by clusters of leaves, leaf 
stems without blades, discoloration, 
freezing, foreign material, disease, in­
sects, mechanical or other means. Spin­
ach on the shown face shall be reasonably 
representative in size and quality of the 
contents of the container.
RULES AND REGULATIONS
(1) Incident to proper grading and 
handling not more than 7 percent, by 
weight, of the spinach in any lot may be 
small pieces of leaves, not more than 3 
percent of the spinach leaves may be 
damaged by clusters, and not more than
3 percent may fail to meet the remaining 
requirements of the grade, including not 
more than 1 percent for serious damage: 
Provided, That no tolerance shall be per­
mitted for sandburs or other kinds of 
burs.
(2) U. S. Grade B shall consist of spin­
ach leaves which meet the requirements 
for U. S. Grade A, except that they shall 
be reasonably clean, and except for the 
increased tolerances for defects specified 
below.
(1) Incident to proper grading and 
handlings not more than 15 percent, by 
weightr of the spinach in any lot may be 
small pieces, not more than 5 percent of 
the spinach leaves may be damaged by 
clusters, and not more than 5 percent 
may fail to meet the remaining require­
ments of the grade, including not more 
than 2 percent for serious damage: 
Provided, That no tolerance shall be per­
mitted for sandburs or other kinds of 
burs.
(b) Off-Grade spinach leaves. Spinach 
leaves which fail to meet the require­
ments of either of the foregoing grades 
shall be Off-Grade spinach leaves.
(c) Definitions. (1) “Similar varietal 
characteristics 0 means that the spinach 
leaves shall be generally of one type, as 
crinkly leaf type, or flat leaf type. No 
mixture of varieties shall be permitted 
which materially affects the appearance 
.  of the lot.
(2) “Fresh” means that the leaves are 
not more than slightly wilted.
(3) “Clean” means that the spinach 
does not show more than a trace of grit, 
sand, dirt, silt, muck or other similar 
water insoluble, inorganic material.
(4) “Well trimmed” means that the 
leaf stems or petioles are not excessively 
long in relation to the size of the leaf 
blades.
(5) “Damage” means any injury or 
defect which materially affects the ap­
pearance, or the edible, shipping or keep­
ing- quality of the individual leaves or of 
the lot as a whole. The following defects 
or any combination of defects the seri­
ousness of which exceeds the amount al­
lowed for any one defect shall be consid­
ered as damage:
4 (i) Clusters, when there are more 
than 3 leaves attached, except that clus­
ters of heart leaves with any number of 
leaves shall not be considered as dam­
aged, provided the length of the longest 
leaf in the cluster is not over 3 inches.
(ii) Leaf stems without blades at­
tached when present to such an extent 
as to materially affect the appearance of 
the lot, or when the individual stem is 
damaged.
(iii) Discoloration, when the appear­
ance of the leaf is materially affected. 
Heart leaves which are yellow or par­
tially blanched shall not be considered 
as damaged by discoloration.
(iv) Mechanical damage, when the 
leaf is very badly crushed, torn, or 
broken. (Owing to the many necessary 
handlings in the harvesting, icing, ship­
ping, sorting, washing, and packing op­
erations In preparing spinach for con­
sumer use some leaves are crushed, torn 
or broken but only those leaves which 
are very badly crushed, torn or broken 
shall be considered as damaged by 
mechanical means.)
(6) “Serious damage” means any in­
jury or defect whjch seriously affects the 
appearance, or the edible, shipping or 
keeping quality of the individual leaves 
or of the lot as a whole. The following 
defects shall be considered as serious 
damage:
(1) Badly discolored leaves.
(ii) Leaves severely affected by mildew 
or white rust.
(iii) Leaves on which insects are pres­
ent, or leaves which are seriously dam­
aged by insects.
(iv) Leaves which are affected by soft 
rot.
(v) Weeds, grass or pieces thereof, 
and other extraneous matter.
(7) “Reasonably clean” means that 
the spinach is reasonably free from grit, 
sand, dirt, silt, muck or other similar 
water insoluble, inorganic material.
(d) Effective time.  The United States 
Consumer Standards for Fresh Spinach 
Leaves contained in this section shall be­
come effective thirty (30) days after the 
date of publication of these standards in 
the F ederal  R egister .
(Pub. Law 266, 80th Cong., 11 F. R. 7713)

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. In the held text of Executive Order 12553 the number 9936 appears in the number column of the first table page, and the aligned entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, matching this order's title. This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Terminal Railroad Association of St. Louis and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of March 18, 1948 (due by April 17, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

WHEREAS a dispute exists between

Its report deadline (April 17, 1948, thirty days after signing on March 18, 1948) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (recitals, creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). Signature, date line and any attached list identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence of Executive Order 12553."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. In the held text of Executive Order 12553 the number 9940 appears in the number column of the first table page, and the aligned entry in the separately extracted subject column (matched by position) describes an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute, matching this order's title. This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Railway Express Agency, Inc., and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of March 25, 1948 (due by April 24, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 9940
Creating an E mergency  B oard to 
I nvestigate a D ispute  B etween  the 
R ailway E xpress  A gency, I nc., and 
Certain of I ts E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Railway Express Agency, Inc., a car­
rier, and certain of its employees repre­
sented by the International Brotherhood  
of Teamsters, Chauffeurs, Warehouse­
men and Helpers of America, AFL, a  
labor organization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt  
interstate commerce to a degree such as  
to deprive a large section of the country  
of essential transportation service: 
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Actr 41s amended (45  
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me, to  
investigate said dispute. No member of  
the said board shall be pecuniarily or  
otherwise interested in any organization  
of employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said  
dispute within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Railway Express Agency,  
Inc., or its employees in the conditions  
out of which the said dispute arose.

Identity: the held Federal Register text is the order itself (heading and body read in full; signed March 25, 1948). Inventory read and confirmed (correction only where stated). End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete with no coverage warning.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (April 24, 1948, thirty days after signing on March 25, 1948) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (recitals, creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). Signature, date line and any attached list identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the full held text of Executive Order 12553, because no acting-provision record for this order is in the packet."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 9948 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Aliquippa and Southern Railroad Company and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of April 10, 1948 (due by May 10, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 9948
Creating an E mergency  B oard to I nvesti ­
gate a D ispute  B etw een The A liquippa  
and S outhern  R ailroad C ompany  and 
Certain of I ts E mployees
WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Aliquippa and Southern Railroad 
Company, a carrier, and certain of its 
employees represented by the Brother­
hood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor or­
ganization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not hereto­
fore been adjusted under the provisions 
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce within the State of 
Pennsylvania to a degree such as to de­
prive that portion of the country of es­
sential transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in' any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said dis­
pute within thirty days from the date of 
this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Aliquippa and Southern 
Railroad Company or its employees in 
the conditions out of which the said dis­
pute arose.

Identity: the held Federal Register text is the order itself (heading and body read in full; signed April 10, 1948). Inventory read and confirmed (correction only where stated). End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete with no coverage warning.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (May 10, 1948, thirty days after signing on April 10, 1948) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (recitals, creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). Signature, date line and any attached list identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the full held text of Executive Order 12553, because no acting-provision record for this order is in the packet."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 9949 with the subject "Amending provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations", and the same table lists Executive Order 9721, the order this one modified. This order modified paragraph 3(a) of Executive Order 9721 for one named employee, Paul D. Miles, so that his reemployment rights applied if his service with the International Frequency Registration Board ended without prejudice within five years of his transfer. Executive Order 10415 later struck the words "within five years from the date of his transfer to such Board" and inserted "on or before December 31, 1953"; that strike-and-insert amendment is a later event, not an end, and the clause continued, amended, until the express revocation. Executive Order 12553 also revokes amendments, so Executive Order 10415 is revoked with it.

by the Civil Service Act (22 Stat. 403) and 
section 1753 of the Revised Statutes, and 
as President of the United States, it is 
ordered that paragraph 3 (a) of Execu­
tive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946, pro­
viding for the transfer of personnel to

which the United States Government 
participates, be, and it is hereby, mod­

ice in the public international organiza­

munications Commission to the Interna­

Union, be entitled to such reemployment 
rights if his service with the said Inter­
national Frequency Registration Board 
is terminated without prejudice within 
five years from the date of his transfer 
to such Board; provided that he complies 
with all other provisions of the said Exec­
utive order With respect to such reem­
ployment.

§  60.1 Ten year guaranteed minimum  
price — (a) Guarantee.  To stimulate do­
mestic5  production of uranium and in the 
interest of the -common defense and se­
curity the United States Atomic Energy 
Commission hereby establishes the guar­
anteed minimum prices specified in par­
agraph (b) of this section, for the de­
livery to the Commission, in accordance 
with the terms of this section during the 
ten calendar years following its effective 
date, of domestic refined uranium, high- 
grade uranium-bearing ores- and me­
chanical concentrates, in not less than 
the quantity and grade specified in par­
agraph (e) of this section. This guaran­
tee does not apply to uranium-bearing 
ores of the Colorado Plateau area, com­
monly known as carnotite-type or ros- 
coelite-type ores, prices for which are 
established by § 60.3.
Note : The term “domestic” in this section,  
referring to uranium, uranium-bearing ores  
and mechanical concentrates, means such  
uranium, ores, and concentrates produced  
from deposits within the United States, its  
territories, possessions and the Canal Zone.
(b) Guaranteed minimum prices.  The 
following minimum prices are estab­
lished:
(1) For uranium-bearing ores and 
mechanical concentrates, $3.50 per 
pound of U3 O s (uranium oxide) deter­
mined by the Commission to be recover­
able, less cost per pound of refining such 
ores or concentrates to standards of 
purity required for the Commission’s 
operations, to be determined by the Com­
mission after assay of a representative 
sample.
(2) For refined uranium products, 
$3.50 per pound contained U3 0 8  (uranium 
oxide).
Prices are f. o. b. railroad cars or trucks 
at shipping point designated by the 
Commission convenient to mine, mill, or 
refinery. Weights are avoirdupois dry 
weight.
(c) MaJcirlg an offer.  Anyone who has 
domestic refined uranium, high-grade 
uranium-bearing ores, or mechanical 
concentrates of the quantity and grade 
specified in paragraph (e) of this sec­
tion, may offer it for delivery to the 
Commission by sending a letter or tele­
gram addressed as follows:
United States Atomic Energy Commission,
Post Office Box 30, Ansonia Station,
New York 23, N. Y.
A ttention: Division of Raw Materials.  
With each offer there should be- fur­
nished a representative ten-pound sam­
ple and the following information:
(1) Location of property;
(2) Character of material offered for 
delivery (state whether refined uranium, 
mechanical concentrates, or uranium­
bearing ores, indicating approximate 
composition);
(3) Amount of material offered;
(4) Location of material offered;
(5) Origin of material If offered by 
other than producer;
(6) If material is owned, in whole or
in part, by any person other than tne 
person making the offer, the name of 
each person having such ownership and 
nature of his rights; and
(7) Name and address of person mak­
ing the offer.
Note : The reporting requirements hereof  
have been approved by the Bureau of the  
Budget pursuant to the Federal Reports Act  
of 1942.
(d) Purchase contract . Upon receipt 
of an offer and sample, aii analysis of 
the sample will be made. If the sample 
and the information furnished are de­
termined by the Commission to meet the 
conditions of this section, the Commis­
sion will forward to the person making 
the offer a form of contract containing 
applicable terms and conditions ready 
for his acceptance. Prices will be not 
less than the applicable prices of para­
graph (b) of this section.
(e) Minimum quantity and grade.  No 
delivery will be accepted under this sec­
tion of less than ten short tons (2,000 
pounds per ton) of ores or mechanical 
concentrates, nor of ore or mechanical 
concentrates which assay less than 10 
per cent U3 0 8  by weight. No delivery will 
be accepted under this section of less 
than one short ton of refined uranium, 
nor of refined uranium which contains 
by weight less than 97 per cent U3 Oa  in 
black uranium oxide or 87 per cent U3 Os  
in sodium uranate. However, the Com­
mission will be interested in negotiating 
reasonable terms with respect to deliv­
eries of high-grade ores and refined 
products in lesser quantities and grades 
than those specified in this section.
(f) Large quantities or special condi­
tions.  The prices established in para­
graph (b) of this section are minimum 
prices. The Commission may by nego­
tiations establish higher prices for guar­
anteed delivery of lots of ores or me­
chanical concentrates substantially in 
excess of ten short tons, or for lots of 
refined uranium substantially in excess 
of one short ton. The Commission also 
may by negotiation establish higher 
prices for delivery of ores, mechanical 
concentrates, or refined uranium under 
other special conditions, taking into con­
sideration such factors as refining and 
milling costs, transportation costs, and 
other applicable factors.
(g) Other valuable minerals.  In 
making payment for material delivered 
to it in accordance with this section, the 
Commission will give consideration to the 
existence of recoverable gold, silver, ra­
dium, thorium, or any other valuable 
constituent in the light of the cost of 
recovery.
(h) Licenses.  Arrangements will be 
made by the Commission for the issuance 
of licenses, pursuant to the Atomic En­
ergy Act of 1946, covering deliveries of 
source material to the Commission under 
this section. (Sec. 5 (b), 60 Stat. 761)
Effective date.  This circular will be­
come effective at midnight, April 11, 
1948.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 10011, signed October 22, 1948 (published October 26, 1948), paragraph 3(b) of which orders that Executive Order 9870 of July 8, 1947, and Executive Order 9982 of July 29, 1948, are hereby revoked. The order states no delayed effective date, so the effective date is the signing date, 1948-10-22. Executive Order 9982 extended and continued the provisions of Executive Order 9870 (foreign service allowances and allotments) to and including June 30, 1949, effective as of July 1, 1948. That own-terms end date (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end the extension when July 1, 1949 begins) was not reached because the express revocation came first. The proviso in paragraph 3(b) keeps rules and regulations prescribed under the revoked orders in effect until superseded under paragraph 3(a); it does not extend the revoked order itself.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 9991 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Pittsburgh & West Virginia Railway Company and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of August 26, 1948 (due by September 25, 1948), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

Creating an E mergency B oard T o I nves ­

WHEREAS a dispute exists between  
the Pittsburgh &  West Virginia Railway 
Company, a carrier, and certain of its  
employees represented by the Brother­
hood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor or­
ganization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce within the States of  
Ohio and Pennsylvania to a degree such  
as* to deprive those states of essential  
transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. ICO), I hereby create a board  
of three members,%to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily  
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.

the President with respect to the said  
dispute within thirty days from the date  
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Pittsburgh &  West Virginia 
Railway Company or its employees in the  
conditions out of which the said dispute  
arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text is the order itself (heading and body read in full; signed August 26, 1948). Inventory read and confirmed (correction only where stated). End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete with no coverage warning.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (September 25, 1948, thirty days after signing on August 26, 1948) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (recitals, creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). Signature, date line and any attached list identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the full held text of Executive Order 12553, because no acting-provision record for this order is in the packet."}

savings_residuals.reason: No saving or transition provision appears in the held text of Executive Order 12553; the order's one-time commands were performed or lapsed, and the statute it applied (Railway Labor Act section 10) continues independently without needing this order.

Inventory read and confirmed: the lead-in and two numbered amendments, with the retroactive effective-date sentence inside the last clause. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, which lists this order by number and also revokes any amendments and the amended Executive Order 10010. Prior research: none reported. It is an amendment to Executive Order 10010, itself ended only by Executive Order 12553 (report deadline and standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling). The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (each complete) and my reading of Executive Order 12553 show no earlier revoking or superseding instrument. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10029 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute". This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between Northwest Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of January 19, 1949 (due by February 18, 1949), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10050 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Railway Express Agency, Inc., and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of April 9, 1949 (due by May 9, 1949), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10056 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Union Railroad Company (Pittsburgh) and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of May 12, 1949 (due by June 11, 1949), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

C reating  an  E m ergency  B oard to I n v e s­
tigate  a D is p u t e B e t w e e n th e M i s­
so u r i P acific  R ailroad  C o m pa n y and

WHEREAS a dispute exists between 
the Missouri Pacific Railroad Company, 
a carrier, and certain of its employees 
represented by the Brotherhood of Loco­
motive Engineers, the Brotherhood of 
Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, 
the Order of Railway Conductors, and 
the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, 
labor organizations; and 
WHEREAS this dispute has not here­
tofore been adjusted under the provi­
sions of the Railway Labor Act, as 
amendéd; and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board, 
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce within several States 
to a degree such as to deprive a large 
portion of the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the 
authority vested in me by section 10 of 
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of 
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to 
the President with respect to the said 
dispute within thirty days from the date 
of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this 
date and for thirty days after the board 
has made its report to the President, no 
change, except by agreement, shall be 
made by the Missouri Pacific Railroad 
Company or its employees in the condi­
tions out of which the said dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12553, signed February 25, 1986, which orders that the listed Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked, with no stated delayed effective date and no saving clause; the effective date is therefore the signing date, 1986-02-25. The table of revoked orders in the held text of Executive Order 12553 lists number 10078 with the subject "Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute". This order created a board of three members to investigate the dispute between the Monongahela Connecting Railroad Company and certain of its employees, barred interested members, required a report within thirty days of September 9, 1949 (due by October 9, 1949), and froze changes in conditions from that date until thirty days after the report. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, the report deadline and the end of the standstill are spent facts, functionally spent after the board reported and the standstill ran, and they are not the end; the order remained on the books until this express revocation.

EXECUTIVE ORDER 10078
Creating an E mergency B oard T o I nves ­
tigate a D ispute  B etween  the Monon - 
gahela C onnecting R ailroad C ompany 
and C ertain of I ts E mployees
WHEREAS s l dispute exists between  
the Monongahela Connecting Railroad  
Company, a carrier, and certain of its  
employees represented by the Brother­
hood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor or­
ganization; and
WHEREAS this dispute has not hereto­
fore been adjusted under the provisions  
of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; 
and
WHEREAS this dispute, in the judg­
ment of the National Mediation Board,  
threatens substantially to interrupt in­
terstate commerce within the State of*  
Pennsylvania to a degree such as to de­
prive that portion of the country of essen­
tial transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the  
authority vested in me by section 10 of  
the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45  
U. S. C. 160), I hereby create a board of  
three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate the said dispute. No mem­
ber of the said board shall be pecuniarily  
or otherwise interested in any organiza­
tion of railway employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to  
the President with respect to the said dis­
pute within thirty days from the date of  
this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Rail­
way Labor Act, as amended, from this  
date and for thirty days after the board  
has made its report to the President, no  
change, except by agreement, shall be  
made by the Monongahela Connecting  
Railroad Company or its employees in the  
conditions out of which the said dispute  
arose.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text is the order itself (heading and body read in full; signed September 9, 1949). Inventory read and confirmed (correction only where stated). End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25 under owner ruling 2026-10-21 (report deadline option C): a report deadline and an expired standstill are not ends. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete with no coverage warning.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order itself contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its report deadline (October 9, 1949, thirty days after signing on September 9, 1949) is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill that runs thirty days after the report is likewise a spent fact under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling; neither is claimed as the end. The actual report date and standstill expiry are not recorded as later events because no reviewed factual-event record for this order's report is in the packet; any report text found in the repository is unreviewed context. The dossier's chain of later events, its three selected machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register catalog dispositions, each marked complete) and my reading of the held text of Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25.","independent_command_check":"Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on the order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence restates section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); that statute is an independent source of duty and is untouched by the revocation, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board and nothing held shows them still running.","savings_check":"Executive Order 12553 was read in full and contains no saving clause. The residual consequences of the order (the board's investigation and report, any settlement of the dispute) are not shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.","scope_check":"One clause is inventoried: the whole operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (recitals, creation of the board, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). Signature, date line and any attached list identify the parties and contain no separate command. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the full held text of Executive Order 12553, because no acting-provision record for this order is in the packet."}

savings_residuals.reason: No saving or transition provision appears in the held text of Executive Order 12553; the order's one-time commands were performed or lapsed, and the statute it applied (Railway Labor Act section 10) continues independently without needing this order.
